description: Hard palate and velum norms (mm) from the anatomical literature, and the same measures taken on the Z-Anatomy skull by experiments/issue-9-palate-za.mjs (numbers only; the meshes are CC BY-SA 4.0 and stay out of the repository).

oraleStaphylion.definition: Palatal (vault) length: orale, the lingual alveolar margin behind the central incisors, to staphylion, the posterior nasal spine, straight.
oraleStaphylion.citation: Tomaszewska IM, Tomaszewski KA, Kmiotek EK, et al. (2014) Anatomical landmarks for the localization of the greater palatine foramen - a study of 1200 head CTs, 150 dry skulls, systematic review of literature and meta-analysis. Journal of Anatomy 225(4), 419-435. doi:10.1111/joa.12221 (PMC4174025), Table 1: 655 men and 695 women over 21 years, CT and dry skulls.

velumLength.definition: Velar length on midsagittal MRI: curvilinear, from the posterior border of the hard palate through the middle of the velum to the tip of the uvula.
velumLength.citation: Perry JL, Kotlarek KJ, Sutton BP, Kuehn DP, Jaskolka MS, Fang X, Point SW, Rauccio F (2016) Variations in velopharyngeal structure in adults with repaired cleft palate. Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Journal 53(1), e1-e13. doi:10.1597/14-015 (PMC7528210), Table 2: the 30 adults without cleft (15 men, 15 women, Caucasian), sexes pooled.

child.citation: Kollara L, Perry JL, Hudson S (2016) Racial variations in velopharyngeal and craniometric morphology in children: an imaging study. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research 59(1), 27-38. doi:10.1044/2015_JSLHR-S-14-0236 (PMC4867931); Table 5: 32 children aged 4-8 years (16 White, 16 Black), estimated marginal means adjusted for head circumference and pooled across race, velar length boys 26.0 and girls 27.4 mm, thickness 7.4 and 7.7 mm (White children 22-23 mm long, Black children 30-32 mm).

velumThickness.definition: Velar thickness on midsagittal MRI, at the velar knee, where the velum is thickest.

zAnatomy.source: Z-Anatomy, Models-of-human-anatomy (https://github.com/Z-Anatomy/Models-of-human-anatomy), CC BY-SA 4.0: maxillae, palatine bones, upper teeth, soft palate and uvula of one specimen, cut at x = +-1.2 mm (the palatine bones stop 0.8 mm short of the midline).
zAnatomy.note: Bone surfaces: the oral mucosa adds about 3 mm under the vault, so the soft-tissue vault is about that much lower. The orale is estimated at the lingual maximum of the incisors.
